s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with a history of transient neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Right ankle clonus and upgoing plantar response
key_facts: 36-year-old man of Indian origin
Presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute symptoms
Awoke around midnight with headache and vomiting
No visual change or speech disturbance
History of odd sensations and occasional tremors in right arm and leg
No medical history
Nonsmoker, denied alcohol or drug use
Normal pulse, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation
Alert with intact speech
Partial left ptosis
Normal cardiorespiratory examination
Noncontrast CT head showed no acute pathology
Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex
Normal CT angiography and CT perfusion
Normal laboratory studies except for total protein of 87 g/L
Normal chest radiograph, 12-lead ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography
Brain MRI showed recent ischemic infarction in left paramedian medulla

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Recent ischemic infarction in left paramedian medulla on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and vomiting with a history of transient neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Moyamoya disease
shortlist.why_kept: Recent ischemic infarction and history of transient neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of headache and vomiting with a history of odd sensations and occasional tremors

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla, which explains the key facts without contradiction.

rejected.label: Cavernous malformation
rejected.why: Although a small frontal cavernoma was noted, it does not explain the acute symptoms and recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla.

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of inflammation or vasculitis on the imaging studies or laboratory results.

rejected.label: Moyamoya disease
rejected.why: There is no evidence of moyamoya disease on the imaging studies, such as CT angiography or MR angiography.

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
rejected.why: There is no evidence of vasoconstriction on the imaging studies, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not support this diagnosis.
